mechanisms.claim: TileLang operand delivery and completion dependencies underfeed tensor compute
mechanisms.code_difference: Lane-issued LDGSTS copies, phase waits and block synchronization versus TMA transfers; current TileLang explicitly disables warp specialization and synchronizes each K tile.
mechanisms.expected_consequences: Lower tensor activity and fewer active warps despite comparable CTA residency ceilings.
observations: TileLang SASS LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128, UTCHMMA, UTCBAR, SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT and BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING
selected_records.json: tensor activity, active warps, launch residency limits; all report range 0/action 0
mechanisms.alternative: Replay/cache differences or tensor-instruction granularity and epilogue costs also contribute; TileLang stall and eligible-warp metrics are uncollected.
mechanisms.limits: No elapsed-time attribution or quantitative share of benchmark gap; TileLang capture-time kernel source missing.

mechanisms.claim: cuTile and Triton are benchmark parity; counters show different scheduling tradeoffs
mechanisms.code_difference: cuTile uses 256 threads and role-specific register deallocation; Triton uses 128 threads and cached B transpose.
mechanisms.expected_consequences: Higher cuTile active occupancy but lower warp instruction issue and eligibility; role-idle waits can be large.
observations: selected_records.json: launch block size, registers, active warps, instructions, eligibility, long-scoreboard ratio; range 0/action 0
mechanisms.alternative: Role-specialized waits prevent interpreting whole-kernel stall averages as useful-compute critical-path stalls.
mechanisms.limits: 8.5% CSV latency difference is within 10% parity convention; no independent claimed cause of that small gap.
